clues: A dense fibrous connective tissue structure in the musculoskeletal system.
It serves as an attachment for broad, flat muscles rather than a round cord.
It is a flat, sheet-like tendon.
A muscle architectural type defined by fiber angle.
Its short fibers attach obliquely along a tendon like feathers.
Unipennate and bipennate muscles belong to this group.
A functional and structural muscle arrangement around a passage.
Its fibers form a ring that narrows or closes a lumen.
A circular muscle around an opening or orifice is this structure.
A functional label given to a muscle during a joint action.
It provides the main force driving the desired movement.
Also called an agonist, it is the chief muscle causing an action.
A functional role defined in opposition to another muscle.
It acts against the motion produced by a prime mover.
A muscle that opposes or slows a given movement has this role.
A muscle that cooperates during coordinated limb or trunk action.
It can assist a prime mover or prevent unwanted motion at a joint.
It works alongside another muscle to smooth or steady movement.
A functional unit of neuromuscular control.
It links nervous excitation directly to a group of contractile fibers.
It consists of one motor neuron and the muscle fibers it innervates.
A specialized peripheral synapse between nerve and muscle.
Neurotransmitter release here triggers muscle fiber depolarization.
Also called the motor end plate, it connects a motor axon to muscle.
A specialized stretch-sensitive proprioceptor inside skeletal muscle.
It lies in parallel with regular extrafusal muscle fibers.
It detects muscle length changes and stretch to drive reflexes.
A proprioceptive sensory ending located outside the muscle belly.
It lies in series with muscle fibers rather than in parallel.
Located in a tendon, it senses muscle tension.
A mode of skeletal muscle activation with cross-bridge activity.
Tension builds in the muscle without changing its overall length.
The muscle contracts against resistance without shortening or lengthening.
A mode of muscle activation often used to control descent.
The muscle generates tension while its overall length increases.
The muscle lengthens while contracting against a load.
